section.content: 本发明涉及对将包含微生物丛的样本进行DNA测序得到的碱基序列进行聚类，以下将上述碱基序列称为样本序列，上述聚类包括以下步骤：对于样本序列，将具有100％的同源性的碱基序列彼此归为一组，由此生成初级OTU(Operational Taxonomic Unit，操作分类单元)；进一步对样本序列进行聚类，由此生成次级OUT，该次级OUT由规定的质心的序列和相对于该规定的质心的序列具有规定的阈值以上的同源性的样本序列构成。其中，规定的阈值小于100％。在各次级OTU所包含的初级OTU中，将序列数最多的初级OTU的序列作为该次级OTU的代表序列，将代表序列与数据库进行比对，由此进行该次级OTU的系统推测。

The present application relates to a method for clustering a base sequence obtained by DNA sequencing a sample containing a microbiota, the base sequence being hereinafter referred to as a sample sequence, the method comprising the steps of: grouping base sequences having 100% homology to each other for the sample sequences, thereby generating primary OTUs (Operational Taxonomic Unit, operation classification unit); the sample sequences are further clustered to generate a secondary OUT composed of a sequence of a predetermined centroid and a sample sequence having homology of a predetermined threshold or more with respect to the sequence of the predetermined centroid. Wherein the prescribed threshold is less than 100%. Among primary OTUs included in each secondary OTU, the sequence of the primary OTU having the largest number of sequences is used as a representative sequence of the secondary OTU, and the representative sequence is aligned with a database, thereby performing system estimation of the secondary OTU.

Metagenomic analysis of microbiotaTechnical Field

The present application relates to metagenomic analysis of microbiota (microbiota), and in particular to meta16S ribosomal RNA (16S rRNA) analysis of bacterial flora, sometimes referred to below as meta16S analysis.

Background

Non-patent document 1 shows that the microbiota, in particular, the bacterial flora (flora) in the uterus affects the success rate of in vitro fertilization. In patent document 1, a specific PCR amplification of the 16S rRNA gene was performed on whole genome DNA extracted from bacteria contained in amniotic fluid using a common primer for the 16S ribosomal RNA gene common to the respective bacteria. Furthermore, it is disclosed that an analysis using Operational Taxonomic Unit (operation classification unit) hereinafter referred to as OUT and other analyses on the amplified products identify chorionic amniotic inflammatory-related microorganisms. Patent document 2 discloses determining the risk of a pregnant woman or a neonate from a bacterial taxa.

Prior art literature

Patent literature

Patent document 1: japanese patent laid-open No. 2018-088843;

patent document 2: japanese patent application laid-open No. 2017-519514.

Non-patent literature

Non-patent document 1: inmaculada Moreno, francisco M.Codoner, felipe Villella, diana Valbuena, juan F.Martinez-Blanch, jorgej jimez-Almazan, roberto Alonso, piclar Alama, jose Remohi, antonio Pellicer, daniel Ramona and Carlos Simon, "Evidence that the endometrial microbiota has an effect on implantation success or failure (how the endometrial microbiota affects implantation success or failure)", american Journal of Obstetrics and Gynecology (journal of gynaecology and obstetrics), 2016, 12 th month 1, volume 215, 6, pages 684-703.

Disclosure of Invention

The inventors devised a method for metagenomic analysis of an intrauterine microbiota and other general microbiota. In this analysis, clustering based on sequence homology thresholds is utilized.

An example of an analytical method designed by the inventors uses so-called exploratory clustering. In exploratory clustering, a change in a cluster to which data should be assigned and a change in the centroid (centroid) of the cluster are repeated. As an example, if there is no change in the allocation of clusters, the process ends here. The cluster at this time was regarded as OTU and the centroid thereof as the representative sequence (Representative Sequence). And comparing the representative sequence with a database to judge the biological species of the OTU.

Such a representative sequence is usually a pseudo sequence, that is, a sequence which is not possessed by a microorganism among the microorganism group in practice, with a high probability. Therefore, an error may occur in the determination of the OTU. The purpose of the present application is to provide a means for reducing the influence of a pseudo sequence when clustering based on a sequence homology threshold is performed in macro genome analysis of a microbiota.

[1] A method of metagenomic analysis of bacterial flora,

clustering a base sequence obtained by DNA sequencing a sample containing bacterial flora, wherein the base sequence is hereinafter referred to as a sample sequence, the clustering comprising the steps of:

for the above sample sequences, base sequences having 100% homology are grouped with each other, thereby generating primary OTUs (Operational Taxonomic Unit, operation classification unit); and

clustering the sample sequences to generate a secondary OTU comprising a sequence of a predetermined centroid and a sample sequence having homology of a predetermined threshold or more to the sequence of the predetermined centroid, wherein the predetermined threshold is less than 100%,

among primary OTUs included in each secondary OTU, the sequence of the primary OTU having the largest number of sequences is used as a representative sequence of the secondary OTU, and the representative sequence is aligned with a database, thereby performing system estimation of the secondary OTU.

[2] The method according to [1], wherein, when the secondary OTU is generated, clusters different from the primary OTU are allocated for the first time to the sample sequence, and the re-allocation of the clusters to the sample sequence having homology equal to or greater than a predetermined threshold value with respect to the sequence of the centroid of the clusters is further repeated until convergence.

[3] The method according to [2], wherein, when a cluster is allocated for the first time to the sample sequence, a seed sequence is randomly selected from the sample sequence, and an initial cluster is allocated to the seed sequence and a sequence having homology of the predetermined threshold or more with respect to the seed sequence.

[4] The method according to [2] or [3], wherein, when the secondary OTU is produced after the primary OTU is produced,

the cluster is a cluster comprising the primary OTU,

the centroid sequence is an average of the primary OTU sequences weighted by the number of primary OTU sequences.

[5] The method according to any one of [2] to [4], wherein when allocation of all clusters is unchanged at the time of reallocating the clusters, the above-described situation is regarded as convergence.

[6] The method according to any one of [1] to [5], wherein the sample is uterine cavity fluid or vaginal swab of the subject,

the sample sequence is produced by DNA sequencing of a partial sequence of the 16S rRNA gene of genomic DNA extracted from the sample,

the database contains the sequences and comments of the 16S rRNA gene of Lactobacillus,

in the above system presumption, the genus of bacteria of the above secondary OTU is presumed,

generating data including the identifier of the subject and the composition ratio of the genus including the bacterium of the genus lactobacillus in the bacterial flora.

[7] The method according to [6], wherein the database further contains sequences and annotations of 16S rRNA genes of Bifidobacterium (Bifidobacterium), propionibacterium (Propionibacterium), gardnerella (Gardnerella), streptococcus (Streptococcus) and Vellonella (Vellonella),

the partial sequence is a sequence of a portion which is not completely conserved among the genus of these bacteria in the entire sequence of the 16S rRNA gene.

[8] The method according to [6] or [7], wherein the database is a database generated by meta-analyzing a plurality of other databases.

[9] A method of collecting uterine cavity fluid or vaginal swab from a subject as said sample,

performing metagenomic analysis on the sample by the method according to any one of [1] to [5], wherein,

the above sample sequence is generated by DNA sequencing of a partial sequence of the 16S rRNA gene of the genomic DNA extracted from the above sample,

the database contains the sequences and comments of the 16S rRNA gene of Lactobacillus,

in the above system presumption, the genus of bacteria of the above secondary OTU is presumed,

diagnosing the susceptibility to conception in the subject based on the ratio of the members of the genus Lactobacillus and the bacteria other than Lactobacillus in the bacterial flora.

[10] A method for metagenomic analysis of a eukaryotic microbiota,

clustering a base sequence obtained by DNA sequencing a sample containing a microbiota, the base sequence being hereinafter referred to as a sample sequence, the clustering comprising the steps of:

grouping base sequences having 100% homology with each other into a group for the above sample sequences, generating a primary OTU (Operational Taxonomic Unit, operation classification unit); and

clustering the sample sequences to generate a secondary OTU comprising a sequence of a predetermined centroid and a sample sequence having homology of a predetermined threshold or more to the sequence of the predetermined centroid, wherein the predetermined threshold is less than 100%,

among primary OTUs included in each secondary OTU, the sequence of the primary OTU having the largest number of sequences is used as a representative sequence of the secondary OTU, and the representative sequence is aligned with a database, thereby performing system estimation of the secondary OTU.

[11] A program for metagenomic analysis of a bacterial or eukaryotic microbiota, said program configured to:

clustering a base sequence obtained by DNA sequencing a sample containing the microbiota, the base sequence being hereinafter referred to as a sample sequence, the clustering comprising the steps of:

grouping base sequences having 100% homology with each other into a group for the above sample sequences, generating a primary OTU (Operational Taxonomic Unit, operation classification unit); and

clustering the sample sequences to generate a secondary OTU comprising a sequence of a predetermined centroid and a sample sequence having homology of a predetermined threshold or more to the sequence of the predetermined centroid, wherein the predetermined threshold is less than 100%,

among primary OTUs included in each secondary OTU, the sequence of the primary OTU having the largest number of sequences is used as a representative sequence of the secondary OTU, and the computer performs system estimation of the secondary OTU by comparing the representative sequence with a database.

The present application can provide a means for reducing the influence of a pseudo sequence when clustering based on a sequence homology threshold is performed in macro genome analysis of a microbiota.

Detailed Description

In this embodiment, metagenomic analysis of microbiota, particularly bacterial flora, is performed. In metagenomic analysis, non-hierarchical clustering, in particular exploratory clustering, is utilized. By utilizing exploratory clustering, a balance between the accuracy of clustering and the computational cost can be achieved. An example of exploratory clustering is k-means.

FIG. 1 is a flow of metagenomic analysis. Each process of metagenomic analysis is mechanically performed by a computer, and may be shared by different computers or may be collectively performed by one computer. In step S11, a sample containing bacterial flora is subjected to DNA sequencing to obtain a base sequence. Hereinafter, this base sequence is referred to as a sample sequence.

In one embodiment, the bacterial flora is harvested from any of the amniotic cavity, the uterine cavity, the cervical canal, and the vagina (vagina). In this specification, "Vagina" is a medical term used as Vagina to represent english and german. In one embodiment, from a cervical swab, a vaginal swab (vaginal swab), a placental swab, and an umbilical cord swab; urine, amniotic fluid, whole blood, serum, plasma, uterine cavity fluid and cervical canal mucus; and extracting DNA as a sample from any of the tissues other than these.

In one embodiment, the DNA sequencer sends the sample sequence to a computer. The computer automatically processes the sample sequence. In other approaches, the DNA sequencer sends a sequence of samples to a server connected via a network. The server records the sample sequence. Upon request by the computer, the server sends a sequence of samples to the computer connected via the network. The computer automatically processes the sample sequence.

Next, in step S12 shown in fig. 1, the sample sequences are grouped according to 100% homology, thereby obtaining a primary OTU (Primary OTU). In one approach, the grouping is performed by exploratory clustering. Next, in step S13, exploratory clustering is performed on the sample sequence with a homology threshold of less than 100%, resulting in secondary OTU (Secondary OTU). Next, in step S14, a system estimation of the representative sequence in the secondary OTU is performed, and thus, the system estimation of the secondary OTU is performed.

The terms "OTU" and Operational Taxonomic Unit (operation classification unit) refer to classification units of living beings obtained when base sequences of living beings are classified on a computer with their similarity as an index. In the case where the organism is a bacterium, for example, the base sequence of the 16S rRNA gene can be used. Whether OTUs are identical to the taxonomic, evolutionary taxonomic, or not, one of the important uses of OTUs is to classify the organisms actually present, e.g., bacteria constituting the bacterial flora, based on OTUs. On the other hand, by performing systematic estimation of OTU, it is possible to associate classification units in the linne taxonomy and the evolutionary taxonomy with OTU. The information of the OTU thus systematically estimated can be easily applied to clinical use.

In step S11 of fig. 1, a sample sequence is obtained. The sample sequence is obtained as a collection of base sequences of various bacteria included in the bacterial flora and of bacteria of each system. The collection of sample sequences contains abundance ratios of bacteria of each genus in the bacterial flora. In addition, each sample sequence is derived from any genus or species. In one embodiment, no systematic presumption of bacteria is made at this time. In one embodiment, the abundance ratio of bacteria of each genus in the bacterial flora is not presumed at this time.

The sample sequence is set to a predetermined length in consideration of the known genome sequence. Among them, the length is not completely uniform in view of the occurrence of deletions and duplications, which also include sequences generated by DNA sequencing errors. The sample sequence can be a genomic sequence with low conservation among species and high conservation among species. In one embodiment, genomic DNA fragments having the sample sequence are cloned using, for example, primers, adaptors.

FIG. 2 exemplarily shows grouping base sequences having 100% homology with each other in a sample sequence. As shown above, OTU a has a sequence of 100 copies, OTU b has a sequence of 10 copies, and OTU c has a sequence of 5 copies. The sequence of OTU b produces a double base substitution (from ATT to AGC) relative to the sequence of OTU a. The sequence of OTU c produces a double base substitution (from ATT to TGT) relative to OTU a. From this grouping, a primary OTU (Operational Taxonomic Unit, operation classification unit) is generated. This grouping is equivalent to clustering with a threshold of 100% of sequence homology. 100% homology means that the sequences are identical over a defined length of the sample sequence.

The lower columns of fig. 2 represent clusters. I.e. represents the primary OTU. The height of each column represents the copy number of each primary OTU. The shorter the distance between the primary OTUs, the higher the sequence homology. In addition, the homology of sequences cannot be expressed accurately on a two-dimensional plane, and thus the drawing is schematic.

In step S12 of fig. 1, the relationship of the sequence of each primary OTU to the Copy Number (Copy Number) of the sequence is ascertained. Hereinafter, the copy number of a sequence may be referred to as the sequence number. In one embodiment, the ratio of the number of sequences between primary OTUs represents the abundance ratio of bacteria having these sequences within the bacterial flora. The same is true in other OTUs than the primary OTU. However, in the present embodiment, the term "copy number" does not necessarily mean that each sample sequence within the primary OTU and other OTUs is a homogeneous sequence obtained from bacteria having the same genome. Sequences other than the sample sequence on the genome sequence may differ from bacterium to bacterium. Thus, bacteria within the primary OTU are presumed to be contained in the taxa, species, genus.

In one embodiment, after the primary OTU is manufactured, the secondary OTU is manufactured. Thus, exploratory clustering was performed in the order shown in fig. 3 to 6.

Fig. 3 schematically shows the initial cluster allocation. Here, for each sample sequence, clusters other than primary OTUs are initially assigned. As the order of cluster allocation, first, a sample sequence as a seed is randomly selected from among the entire sample sequences, hereinafter referred to as a seed sequence. The primary OTU is essentially randomly selected from among the primary OTU population.

In one mode shown in fig. 3, primary OTU (Pr 1) is selected as the seed sequence. The dashed circle represents a similar range as seen from the primary OTU (Pr 1). That is, the sequence shows a range having homology equal to or greater than a predetermined threshold value with respect to the sequence of the primary OTU (Pr 1). The range is assigned an initial cluster.

As shown in fig. 3, a primary OTU (Pr 2) different from the primary OTU (Pr 1) is included in a similar range. Thus, the primary OTU (Pr 1) and primary OTU (Pr 2) are assigned initial clusters. The columns are shaded to indicate primary OTUs assigned to the same cluster. These primary OTUs constitute a cluster. In the other figures, hatching indicates the same meaning.

Although not illustrated in fig. 3, other primary OTUs that are not similar to the primary OTU (Pr 1) are equally allocated into other clusters. As above, clusters containing primary OTUs are generated.

Fig. 4 schematically shows the reassignment of clusters. Centroid Ct1 is the centroid of the cluster, namely the centroids of primary OTU (Pr 1) and primary OTU (Pr 2). The dotted circle represents a similar range as seen from the centroid Ct 1. That is, the sequence having a homology equal to or greater than a predetermined threshold value with respect to the centroid Ct1 is shown. Clusters are reassigned to primary OTUs (Pr 3) within a similar range of newly generated centroids Ct 1.

Fig. 5 schematically shows allocation of duplicate clusters. Centroid Ct2 is the centroid of the cluster with primary OTU (Pr 3), i.e., the centroids of primary OTU (Pr 1), primary OTU (Pr 2), and primary OTU (Pr 3). The dotted circle represents a similar range as seen from the centroid Ct 2. That is, the sequence having a homology equal to or greater than a predetermined threshold value with respect to the centroid Ct2 is shown. Clusters are reassigned to primary OTUs (Pr 4) within a similar range of newly generated centroids Ct 2.

In this embodiment, the cluster reassignment is repeated until the cluster converges. Thereby, a secondary OTU is generated.

Fig. 6 schematically shows the determination of the secondary OTU (Sc) and representative sequences. Centroid Ct3 is the centroid of the cluster with primary OTU (Pr 4), i.e., the centroids of primary OTU (Pr 1), primary OTU (Pr 2), primary OTU (Pr 3), and primary OTU (Pr 4). The dotted circle represents a similar range as seen from centroid Ct 3. That is, the sequence having a homology equal to or greater than a predetermined threshold value with respect to the centroid Ct3 is shown. Even if clusters are reassigned to a range where newly generated centroids Ct3 are similar, the combination of primary OTUs constituting the clusters does not change. Thus, it can be seen that the cluster converges before the centroid Ct3 is obtained.

Exploratory clustering was performed as above. In exploratory clustering, the specified threshold for homology is less than 100%. In one embodiment, the threshold is an arbitrary value of 90% or more. In one embodiment, the threshold is any of 91, 92, 93, 94, 95, 96, 97, 97.5, 98, 98.5, 99, and 99.5%. The analysis accuracy can be improved by lowering the threshold value. The resolution can be increased by increasing the threshold. Furthermore, the calculation time can be reduced.

The cluster obtained as a result of convergence of the exploratory cluster is OTU. In this embodiment, it is referred to as a secondary OTU (Sc). Here, it should be noted that the cluster obtained in the middle of exploratory clustering is also OTU. The cluster consisting of the initial randomly selected seed and the sample sequence similar thereto is an OTU.

The number of cluster reassignments performed until convergence is 1 or more. In the above embodiment, the process was performed 2 times. This number is sometimes 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, and 9. In one embodiment, an upper limit is set on the number of reassignments. In one approach, cluster convergence is presumed when the number of reassignments reaches an upper limit.

In one approach shown in fig. 4-6, the sequence of centroids of clusters is a simple arithmetic average of the sequence of each primary OTU. In other aspects, the sequence of centroids of a cluster is an average of the weighted sequences of primary OTUs with the number of sequences of primary OTUs.

Upon convergence, the secondary OTUs are allowed to contain 1 primary OTU. In addition, all primary OTUs are allowed to be identical to all secondary OTUs.

In one embodiment shown in fig. 6, cluster convergence is estimated when all clusters including clusters not shown are unchanged by reassignment of clusters based on centroid. In another aspect, when the amount of change in the combination of primary OTUs in all clusters is smaller than a predetermined value, the case is regarded as convergence.

In fig. 3, primary OTU (Pr 1) was used as seed. Then, an initial cluster is determined from the seed. In contrast, a group of a plurality of primary OUT groups randomly selected without considering the sequence homology may be used as the initial cluster.

In step S14 shown in fig. 1, a representative sequence of each secondary OTU is first selected for system estimation. In one embodiment, among the primary OTUs included in each secondary OTU, the sequence of the primary OTU having the largest number of sequences is used as the representative sequence of the secondary OTU. In one embodiment shown in fig. 6, the number of sequences of the primary OTU (Pr 3) is the largest among the secondary OTUs (Sc). Thus, the representative sequence of the secondary OTU (Sc) is the sequence of the primary OTU (Pr 3).

In step S14 shown in fig. 1, the representative sequence is further aligned with the database. From the above, system speculation for the secondary OTU is performed. In one embodiment, the systematic speculation is performed on any taxonomic group among phylum, class, order, family, genus, species, and subspecies of bacteria of the secondary OTU.

In one form, the database is a public database. In other aspects, the database is a database generated by Meta-analysis (Meta analysis) of one or more other databases. In one embodiment, the database is connected to the computer via a network.

In meta-analysis, for example, sequences in other databases are distinguished between sequences that are correctly annotated and sequences that are not correctly annotated. In one embodiment, the correctly annotated sequence is the sequence of the model Strain (Type Strain). In one embodiment, the database generated by meta-analysis does not contain multiple identical sequences. By optimizing the database as described above, the calculation cost for aligning the representative sequence with the database can be significantly reduced. In one embodiment, only the highest hit (top hit) is calculated.

< embodiment >

FIG. 7 schematically shows 16S rRNA genes having a base length of about 1500 bp. In this example, DNA having a partial sequence of the 16S rRNA gene was used as a sample. The 16S rRNA gene has 9 hyper-variable regions, hereinafter referred to as variable regions, and regions, hereinafter referred to as conserved regions, existing therebetween. The partial sequence consists of a 300bp region comprising two 5' side variable regions.

In this example, DNA having the above partial sequence was cloned from the uterine cavity fluid or vaginal swab of a subject. These swabs contain a characteristic bacterial flora. And (3) taking the obtained DNA as a sample to carry out DNA sequencing, thereby obtaining a sample sequence. DNA sequencing was performed using a second generation sequencer.

The number of sequences output from the second generation sequencer is very large. By performing the above clustering, homology search in the database is not required for all sequences. In one view, this is because all sample sequences within the secondary OTU can be systematically extrapolated by homology searching of the representative sequence.

Fig. 8 shows a flow of metagenome analysis after sequence determination. First, in step S81, the linker sequence is removed from the original Data (Raw Data) of the sequence, thereby obtaining clean FASTQ-form Data (clean FASTQ). A program named trimmatic can be utilized. The present data and the following data each contain an identifier of the subject.

In step S82 shown in fig. 8, the data (fused FASTQ) in the FASTQ form is obtained by merging the reads (reads) in the data in the FASTQ form. A program with a program name fastq-join can be utilized.

In step S83 shown in fig. 8, the primer sequences in the FASTQ-format data are removed. Further, in step S84, the FASTQ-format data is converted into FASTA-format data. These steps can utilize a program called PRINSEQ.

In step S85 shown in fig. 8, a primary OTU is fabricated from a sample sequence included in FASTA-form data. UCLUST can be utilized under the program name Qiame pick otus. The threshold for homology (similarity) was set to 1.00 (100%). Further, in step S86, sequence information is extracted from each primary OTU. A program named Qiime pick rep set.py can be utilized.

In step S87 shown in fig. 8, a secondary OTU is fabricated from the sample sequence. A program named Qiime pick otus.py can be utilized. The threshold for homology (similarity) was set to 0.995 (99.5%). Further, the primary OTU having the largest number of sequences is selected from among the primary OTUs included in the secondary OTUs, and the sequence is used as a representative sequence.

In this example, for exploratory clustering, UCLUST of Qiame pick otus.py was used. In other embodiments, exploratory clustering is performed by a platform other than the above. Examples of the platform include a user, a CD-HIT, and a vsearch.

In step S88 shown in fig. 8, the representative sequence is aligned with the Database (DB), and data (Assigned txt) in which system information is Assigned to each secondary OTU is generated. Programs named BLAST can be utilized. And further removes low quality reads from the data in step S89.

The Database (DB) used in this example contains the sequence and annotation of the 16S rRNA gene of Lactobacillus. In other embodiments, the database further comprises sequences and annotations of 16S rRNA genes of Bifidobacterium (Bifidobacterium), propionibacterium (Propionibacterium), gardnerella (Gardnerella), streptococcus (Streptococcus) and Veilonella (Veilonella). In this manner, the above partial sequences are not completely conserved among the genus of these bacteria. In one embodiment, the partial sequence is a sequence of a portion having low conservation among the sequences of the whole 16S rRNA. In one embodiment, the conservation of the partial sequences is low enough to distinguish the genus of these bacteria.

Examples of other databases are NCBI, greenGenes, SILVA, ezBioCloud and Ribosomal Database Project. In other embodiments, the database is a meta-analysis of other databases. Examples of other databases are the databases exemplified above. The database generated by meta-analysis of the above-described exemplary databases may include chimeras and misnotes. By using a partial sequence of the 16S rRNA gene as described above, the effects of chimerism and misannotation can be reduced as compared with the case of using a full-length sequence. In addition, the computational cost can be reduced over when using full-length sequences.

From the obtained data (Assigned txt), data containing the composition ratio of bacteria in the bacterial flora and the identifier of the subject are obtained. In one embodiment, the composition ratio of bacteria is proportional to the number of sequences of the secondary OTU. The classification of the bacteria is annotated in the secondary OTU. In one embodiment, the composition ratio of bacteria is, for example, the composition ratio of the genus lactobacillus and the genus bacteria other than the genus lactobacillus in the bacterial flora as shown in fig. 9.

In one embodiment, the computer provides the diagnostician with a composition ratio of bacteria and an identifier of the subject. In one embodiment, the information is provided by a server and a terminal of a diagnostician connected via a network. The diagnostician diagnoses the conception easiness of the in vitro fertilization and the conception easiness of the natural conception of the subject according to the composition ratio of the bacterial flora.

Reference example 1 >

Fig. 10 shows the case of exploratory clustering of sample sequences without making the primary OTUs. Centroid Ct4 is similar to sequences Sq1, sq2, and Sq3 that constitute a cluster. However, centroid Ct4 is a pseudo sequence. That is, centroid Ct4 is a sequence not included in the sample.

In the case of performing the system speculation of the OTU by comparing the centroid Ct4 shown in fig. 10 with the database, the system speculation may be erroneous. This tendency is particularly remarkable in the 16SrRNA gene having high conservation in the whole bacterial classification. In other words, erroneous annotation easily occurs. Therefore, the threshold is preferably set to about 97%. Such a threshold value is suitable for the case where bacteria are systematically estimated by genus or class larger than genus.

In contrast, in the above embodiment, the use of exploratory clustering is the same as in the above embodiment. However, since the representative sequence is selected from the sequences of the primary OTUs within the secondary OTUs, no systematic presumption is made using the dummy sequence. Therefore, the influence of the dummy sequence can be reduced. In addition, in the above embodiment, a sample sequence that generates an error in DNA sequencing can also be introduced into the secondary OTU. Thus, the number of sequences contained in the secondary OTU well represents the entity of the sample, bacterial flora. In the metagenomic analysis of the above embodiment, systematic estimation can be performed more precisely than in metagenomic analysis in which only exploratory clustering is performed.

In addition, errors in sequencing are also background in generating primary OTUs that are similar in sequence to each other. For example, in the case shown in fig. 2, OTU a can be considered to be constituted by a sample sequence having a true sequence, and OTU b and OTU c are constituted by a sample sequence containing errors. In fig. 3 to 6, the secondary OTU is fabricated while the sample sequence containing the error is introduced. However, since the representative sequence is produced from the primary OTU having the largest number of sequences, the accuracy of the systematic estimation of bacteria can be improved.

OTUs, among which sub OTUs are generated according to a sample sequence having 100% homology, can also be generated according to the method of the present reference example. In this sub OUT, the sequence of the sub OTU having the largest number of sequences may be used as a representative sequence. That is, the order of generation of the primary OTU and the secondary OTU in the above-described embodiment may be reversed.

Preferably, in accordance with the above embodiments, the secondary OTU is produced after the primary OTU is produced. Thus, the calculation of the repetition between the completely identical sequences in the primary OTU can be omitted in the generation of the secondary OTU.

Reference example 2 >

In the above embodiment, the primary OTU and the secondary OTU are fabricated using a non-hierarchical clustering method called exploratory clustering, thereby balancing the accuracy of clustering with the computational cost. As a method different from this, it is exemplified that the sample sequences are clustered by hierarchical clustering so that OTUs are generated without using a hierarchical method of generating primary OTUs and secondary OTUs.

Examples of hierarchical clustering include Single link, complete link, and Average link. In the case where the step method of generating the primary OTU and the secondary OTU is not used, in Single linkage, the OTU is very large, and thus it is difficult to improve the accuracy. In the Complete linkage, small OTUs are produced in large quantities without using the stepwise method. Thus, comparison to a database requires computational costs. In the Average linkage, a moderate number of OTUs can be generated in a moderate size without using the stepwise method. However, since the stepwise method is not used, the calculation cost itself associated with the hierarchical clustering becomes very high. In addition, in any hierarchical clustering method, in the case where a centroid is selected as a representative sequence without using a stepwise method, the representative sequence is also generally a pseudo sequence.

The stepwise method of generating primary OTUs and secondary OTUs using exploratory clustering utilized in the above-described embodiments is excellent in the balance of accuracy and computational cost as compared to the method of generating OTUs in one step using hierarchical clustering. In the above embodiment, the representative sequence is selected from the primary OTUs in the secondary OTUs, and therefore, no systematic estimation is performed using the dummy sequence. Therefore, the influence of the dummy sequence can be reduced.
